overview.title: Context in a single visit
overview.p1: Tetouan’s Archaeological Museum gives the region a timeline: Roman-era objects, local excavations and displays that explain why this corridor mattered long before the Andalusian medina.
overview.p2: It is small enough to see properly in under an hour. That makes it ideal between a medina morning and an afternoon craft walk.
overview.p3: Check opening times the same morning — public museums in Morocco can shift hours around holidays.

q1.question: Is there a ticket?
q1.answer: Yes — small public museum fee. Carry cash as backup.

q2.question: How long?
q2.answer: Forty-five to seventy-five minutes is enough for most visitors.

q3.question: Open every day?
q3.answer: Hours vary; confirm the same day, especially around public holidays.

q4.question: Worth it if short on time?
q4.answer: Yes if you like context. Skip only if you have a single half-day in the city.

q5.question: Photos allowed?
q5.answer: Rules vary by room — follow staff guidance.

food.title: Eat around the museum
food.p1: No need to eat inside. Use nearby cafés or return to Place Hassan II.
food.p2: A museum-morning plus medina lunch is a clean day structure.
